extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, Registration Agencies, and apprenticeship program administrators/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for registered apprenticeship program standards, recordkeeping, employer/sponsor obligations, and the contents and administration of apprenticeship agreements under proposed revisions to 29 CFR part 29. Focused on transparency, accountability, worker protections, and data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum on-the-job training hours while allowing advanced standing based on competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Require a minimum amount of on-the-job training hours while allowing advanced standing based on existing competency/ prior experience; combine benefits of competency attainment with minimum employment duration requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is similar to the current “hybrid” model and is intended to balance time-based training to industry standard with recognition of unique skill/competency progressions. Ensures apprentices do not receive an abbreviated OJT experience unless warranted and prevents premature graduation before requisite proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards must address transfer of apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of apprenticeship must include a provision addressing the transfer of apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive elements carried forward require a transferring apprentice be provided a transcript of related instruction and on-the-job learning, transfer to the same occupation, and sign a new apprenticeship agreement when the transfer occurs. Proposed §29.8(a)(21) updates language for clarity but retains these substantive elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping by program sponsors and participating employers (including participating employers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors and participating employers must maintain apprenticeship records (including participating employers) detailing apprentices' interactions with employers and program outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding participating employers enables collection of data such as whether the apprentice was hired, interim credentials earned, the apprentice's wage upon hire, and other key data. The proposal cross-references proposed §29.18 for recordkeeping requirements and clarifies maintenance of specified records for five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period and cross-reference to §29.18
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace prior language about recordkeeping with a cross-reference to proposed §29.18 and require program sponsors and participating employers to maintain required records for five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhancements to recordkeeping are intended to develop a comprehensive national dataset to inform oversight and improvement of the National Apprenticeship System. This clarifies what records must be kept and the retention timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to EEO requirements (29 CFR part 30 or approved State EEO plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of apprenticeship must include a statement that the program must be conducted, operated, and administered in conformity with 29 CFR part 30, as amended, or, if applicable, an approved State EEO plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.8(a)(23) replicates current equal opportunity requirements; apprenticeships must explicitly commit to applicable federal/state EEO obligations as part of program standards and agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining a safe and inclusive workplace free from violence, harassment, intimidation, and retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors and participating employers must promote and maintain a safe and inclusive workplace environment that is free from violence, harassment, intimidation, and retaliation against apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes an obligation to develop and implement procedures to ensure apprentices are not harassed and the program is free from intimidation and retaliation. Failure to comply may be grounds for Registration Agency sanctions, including deregistration and law enforcement referral where appropriate. Intended to deter climates of fear that deter reporting or organizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for failure to abide by standards of apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Noncompliance with the standards of apprenticeship can be grounds for a Registration Agency to impose sanctions against program sponsors or participating employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions could include initiation of deregistration proceedings and referral to law enforcement agencies, as appropriate. Used to enforce requirements such as safe workplace, EEO, and other standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation for compliance with Support for Veterans in Effective Apprenticeships Act
rubrics_metrics.description: For apprenticeship programs registered on or after September 22, 2020, standards of apprenticeship must include an attestation that the program sponsor will provide each of the written assurances required under sec. 2(b)(1) of the Support for Veterans in Effective Apprenticeships Act of 2019 (Pub. L. 116-134).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory requirement has previously been implemented via information collection requests but is proposed to be included in regulatory text because it is a statutory obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify contact information of individual authorized to receive/process complaints (including email)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of apprenticeship must identify contact information for the individual with authority in the program to receive, process, and make disposition of complaints; an email address is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.8(a)(26) makes email a requirement (current rule only says 'if appropriate'). This improves accessibility for apprentices seeking to file or follow up on complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group program employer attestation to abide by parts 29 and 30 prior to admission
rubrics_metrics.description: Group program sponsors must ensure that each participating employer provides an attestation, required prior to admission, that the employer will abide by the requirements in parts 29 and 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.8(b) synchronizes minimum standards with §29.11 Program Standards Adoption Agreement. The attestation is required prior to employer admission to help hold employers and sponsors accountable and protect apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of employer past violations and remedial actions in attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Attestation must disclose whether the participating employer has violated applicable laws governing workplace practices or conduct and any actions taken to remedy violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure would not automatically prevent registration or entry into the program, but Registration Agencies should know of prior violations for oversight. Failure to disclose could result in referral to DOJ for potential 18 U.S.C. §1001 violations if knowingly and willfully false.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor monitoring of participating employers for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Group program sponsors must monitor participating employers for their compliance with the minimum standards of apprenticeship and other requirements in parts 29 and 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.8(b)(3) creates an accountability mechanism to further apprentice safety and welfare, enabling Registration Agencies to hold sponsors responsible. Sponsors may need staff coordinators to coordinate program partners and employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written apprenticeship agreement required and timing of signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: All registered apprenticeship programs must develop a written apprenticeship agreement containing terms and conditions of employment and training, signed by the parties prior to the start of the apprenticeship term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(a) retains and reorganizes existing §29.7 language and adds that for group programs a participating employer signatory is required. Signature prior to start ensures apprentices can review terms before beginning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide proposed agreement and program standards prior to signing and deliver executed copies by start date
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to signing the apprenticeship agreement, sponsors must furnish admitted apprentices with a copy of both the proposed apprenticeship agreement and the program's standards of apprenticeship and provide a reasonable opportunity to inspect and review them; after signing, sponsors must deliver the executed agreement and standards to the apprentice not later than the starting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(b) is intended to mitigate imbalance of bargaining power and procedural unconscionability; Department did not specify a uniform minimum review time to preserve flexibility but invites comment on whether to set one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice identifying/contact information (DOB and voluntary SSN)
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include apprentice contact information and identifying information, including the apprentice's date of birth and, on a voluntary basis, their Social Security number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of birth and voluntary SSN align with current requirements. Apprentices may not be denied entry or subjected to adverse action if they refuse to disclose their SSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for Registration Agency, program sponsor, and participating employer(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must contain contact information for the Registration Agency, the program sponsor, and the participating employer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(2) adds participating employers' contact information only for those signatory at time of signing; agreements need not be re-signed when new participating employers join, though Department seeks comment on transparency vs. administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include occupation, work process schedule, and related instruction outline
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include the occupation in which the apprentice is to be trained as well as the associated work process schedule and related instruction outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carries forward existing §29.7 requirements so apprentices understand the training content and schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate program standards into the apprenticeship agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The program's standards of apprenticeship must be incorporated into the apprenticeship agreement either directly or by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement (from current §§29.5(b)(11) and 29.7(i)) makes compliance with standards part of the contract without requiring verbatim repetition of standards if incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe respective roles, duties, and responsibilities of parties and provide rights/complaint information
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must describe the roles, duties, and responsibilities of the parties, including the responsibility of sponsors and participating employers to provide information to apprentices about their rights and protections under Federal, State, and local laws and the right to file complaints with the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(5) emphasizes clear party responsibilities and aligns with ILO Recommendation to clearly define parties' roles; explicit complaint and rights info improves apprentice protection and access to remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify program dates and probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must contain the beginning date and expected duration of the apprenticeship program, the beginning date of the on-the-job training, and the duration of any probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(6) ensures apprentices have complete information on timing of program components, including when paid OJT begins and the length of probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed wage schedule and fringe benefits tied to competency attainment
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include a detailed statement of the entry wage, subsequent graduated scale of increasing wages corresponding to attainment of occupational skills and competencies, the journeyworker wage, and any fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(7) aligns wage increases with specific skill/competency attainment periods to provide explicit notice of cadence of wage increases and fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected minimum hours for on-the-job training and related instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must disclose the expected minimum number of hours allocated to the on-the-job training component and the related instruction component during the apprenticeship term (may include an approximate range).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(8) replaces existing §29.7(e) and aligns with program standards requiring minimum duration to ensure apprentices understand time expectations for achieving proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe methods to measure progress on competency attainment and end-point assessment (inclusive and accessible)
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include a description of the methods used to measure progress on competency attainment and the program's end-point assessment; methods should be inclusive and accessible to apprentices with disabilities and underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(9) corresponds to proposed §29.8(a)(10) and (11) on regular and end-point assessments and increases transparency so apprentices understand continuous and final evaluation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe available supportive services
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include a description of any supportive services that may be available to the apprentice, including childcare, transportation, equipment, tools, or other supports provided by the sponsor or partner organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(10) informs apprentices of supports that may enable participation (potentially coordinated with workforce development systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose any unreimbursed costs, expenses, or fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must disclose the nature and amount of any unreimbursed costs, expenses, or fees that the apprentice may incur during participation in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(11) corresponds with program standards at §29.8(a)(18) to protect apprentices from hidden or arbitrary costs and aid financial planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe recognized postsecondary credits, credentials, and licensing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must describe any recognized postsecondary credits, credentials, occupational qualifications, or licenses the apprentice will receive or be eligible for upon completion, and any additional conditions required for federal, state, or local qualifications and licensure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(12) provides notice of program outcomes and any extra steps needed to meet occupational licensure or credentialing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation of adherence to 29 CFR part 30 and applicable State EEO plans within the agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must contain a statement that the parties will adhere to the applicable requirements of 29 CFR part 30 as amended and, where applicable, an approved State EEO plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(13) replaces prior equal opportunity language with an explicit reference to part 30 to clarify expectations for sponsors and employers to adhere to all applicable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure about pay and fringe benefits for related instruction and whether such instruction is during work hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Apprenticeship agreements must state whether apprentices are paid wages and any fringe benefits during the related instruction component, what the wage rate and fringe benefits are, and whether related instruction is provided during work hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(14) gives apprentices clarity on compensation during related instruction, enabling financial planning and understanding of paid/unpaid training time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for party to address complaints within the program
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must include contact information of the appropriate party to address complaints within the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(15) ensures apprentices know whom to contact for program-level complaints; apprentices may also file complaints with Registration Agencies under proposed §29.17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe processes and procedures to grant advanced standing or credit
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement must describe the processes and procedures the sponsor will use to grant advanced standing or credit to apprentices; these must be the same as in the sponsor's approved standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(c)(16) ensures apprentices are aware of how advanced standing is granted before signing and that procedures are consistent with approved standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit non-compete provisions that restrict apprentice labor market mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and participating employers are prohibited from including or imposing non-compete provisions or similar provisions that would restrict an apprentice's ability to seek or accept employment with another employer prior to completion of the apprenticeship program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(d) aims to protect apprentices' labor mobility and economic opportunity; non-competes that restrict mobility are impermissible because they undermine apprenticeship goals and harm workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit non-disclosure provisions that hinder ability to work in field or file complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and participating employers are prohibited from including non-disclosure provisions that would prevent the worker from working in the same field after employment or that would restrict an apprentice's ability to file a complaint with a Registration Agency or other governmental body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.9(e) recognizes non-disclosure provisions can silence workers and impede reporting of harassment, discrimination, or rights violations; prohibition promotes accountability and access to remedies.
